cases.quote: ‘ 2018 LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK 左シングル引用符，左シングルクォーテーションマーク used in horizontal composition / 横組で使用
cases.rationale: The first row of §A.1, quoted in the document's own column order — Character 字形, UCS, Name UCS名称, Common name 通用名称, Remarks 備考 — and one of only three rows of the sixteen whose Remarks cell is not empty. The same key is listed a second time under §A.27, where its Remarks cell reads "proportionally-spaced" / 「プロポーショナル」, and that qualification is the one thing separating the two listings; §3.1.2 states that the character advance of opening brackets (cl-01) is half-width, so an occurrence declared on the half em frame satisfies §A.1's listing and not §A.27's. The Remarks cell states a writing mode and not a class: §3.1.1 restricts where this mark is used, and then states an exception — in vertical writing mode, when Western characters (cl-27) are composed rotated 90 degrees clockwise, these quotation marks are sometimes used — so a case that read "used in horizontal composition" as a rule about membership would assert more than the document does. This case therefore sets the mark in the writing mode the Remarks cell names and conditions nothing on it.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.1, first row, against §A.27's Remarks column (§3.9.1, §3.9.2)

forbidden.why: §A.27 lists 2018 with the Remarks cell "proportionally-spaced" / 「プロポーショナル」. This occurrence declares the half em frame, so the sentence that would put it in cl-27 does not describe it. §3.9.1 asks whether the character width is full-width, half-width or something else before any other question, which is why the answer may not be reached without reading the declared frame.

cases.quote: Though REVERSED DOUBLE PRIME QUOTATION MARK "〝" and LOW DOUBLE PRIME QUOTATION MARK "〟" are similar to double quotation marks in appearance (see Figure 62) they are exclusively used for vertical writing mode and are not to be used in horizontal writing mode. / これは，縦組専用の括弧類であり，横組では使用しない．
cases.rationale: The last row of §A.1, and the third of the three rows whose Remarks cell is not empty: "used in vertical composition" / 「縦組で使用」. §3.1.1 states the same restriction a second time, in both locales, and extends it to this mark's cl-02 partner U+301F, so the vertical-only reading of U+301D rests on two sections rather than on one table cell. Membership itself is unconditional and unambiguous: cl-01 is the only Appendix A table that lists 301D, so nothing has to be separated here and the declared frame decides nothing about the class — it is declared because §3.1.2 makes the frame of a cl-01 member a geometry the caller owns, and an unstated one would have no answer to report. This case sets the mark in the only writing mode the document permits it in; the case below sets it in the other one.

cases.quote: Though REVERSED DOUBLE PRIME QUOTATION MARK "〝" and LOW DOUBLE PRIME QUOTATION MARK "〟" are similar to double quotation marks in appearance (see Figure 62) they are exclusively used for vertical writing mode and are not to be used in horizontal writing mode. / これは，縦組専用の括弧類であり，横組では使用しない．
cases.rationale: The same member, the same declared frame, and the writing mode the quoted sentence says it is not used in — and the same answer, which is the point. §A.1 lists 301D unconditionally; what §3.1.1 and the Remarks cell restrict is the use of the mark, not its membership. Measured over the whole appendix exactly twelve keys carry a writing-mode Remark — 2018, 201C and 301D in cl-01, 2019, 201D and 301F in cl-02, 003B in cl-05, 002E in cl-06, 002C in cl-07, and 3033, 3034 and 3035 in cl-08 — and for none of them does the writing mode separate two candidate classes, because every one of them is either sole-listed or separated by the frame. So the direction is a validity fact a caller reads separately and never a class selector, and an implementation that answers differently in the two writing modes has made it one. This case does not assert that the composition is well advised; it asserts what class the occurrence has when a caller writes it anyway, which is the question a classifier is asked.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.1, last row; §3.1.1 restricts the use and not the listing

forbidden.why: The answer an implementation gives when it drops a listing whose Remarks cell names the other writing mode and then falls back on the reading for a code point Appendix A does not list. §A.1's row for 301D is not conditioned on a writing mode, and §3.1.1 says the mark is not to be used horizontally, not that it belongs to another class there.

cases.quote: 「 300C LEFT CORNER BRACKET 始めかぎ括弧
cases.rationale: The ninth row of §A.1 and the ordinary Japanese quotation bracket. Nine of §A.1's sixteen keys are listed by cl-01 and by no other class — 3008, 300A, 300C, 300E, 3010, 2985, 3018, 3016 and 301D — and they are the members whose answer needs no axis at all; this is one of them, and its Remarks cell is empty in both locales, so §A.1 qualifies it by nothing: not by frame, not by writing mode, not by role. The frame is declared because §3.1.2 states that the character advance of opening brackets (cl-01) is half-width and that the conditional space beside them is what "makes them appear as if they were intrinsically full-width", so on a cl-01 member the frame names a geometry rather than a class and an unstated one has no answer to report. No writing mode is declared: §3.1.1 names 「 and 」 as the quotation brackets of vertical composition and records that their adoption in horizontal composition seems to be increasing, and neither sentence is about class.

cases.quote: ｟ 2985 LEFT WHITE PARENTHESIS 始め二重パーレン，始め二重括弧
cases.rationale: The twelfth row of §A.1, quoted exactly as the document prints it — and the glyph in its Character 字形 column is U+FF5F FULLWIDTH LEFT WHITE PARENTHESIS while its UCS column reads 2985. Four of §A.1's sixteen rows do this: U+FF08 stands against 0028, U+FF3B against 005B, U+FF5B against 007B, and U+FF5F against 2985. The key is the UCS cell, and this case supplies U+2985 itself. The failure it exists to catch is silent and passes every count: an extractor keyed on the Character column gives cl-01 sixteen members, agrees on the cardinality, and has four of them wrong. §A.1's Remarks cell for this row is empty in both locales and no other Appendix A table lists 2985, so nothing separates and nothing qualifies — the answer is the listing.

forbidden.why: The answer of an implementation keyed on §A.1's Character 字形 column, for which U+FF5F is the member and U+2985 is a code point no table lists; an unlisted occurrence declared on a frame other than the proportional one then resolves to cl-19 under §3.9.2's silence. §A.1's key is the UCS cell, and a glyph the document printed to show what the member looks like is not one.

cases.quote: warichu opening brackets (cl-28) and warichu closing brackets (cl-29) are used for surrounding inline cutting notes and the space. They are in a separate class since they differ from normal brackets with regard to their processing. / 割注始め括弧類（cl-28）又は割注終わり括弧類（cl-29）は，割注を囲むために用いる括弧類及び空き量のことである．
cases.rationale: U+005B is named by three Appendix A tables — §A.1, §A.27 with the Remarks cell "proportionally-spaced" / 「プロポーショナル」, and §A.28 — and the two axes that separate them are both declared by this input. The half em frame excludes the cl-27 listing, by §3.1.2's half-width advance for cl-01 against §A.27's Remark. The cl-28 listing is excluded by the construct, and the quoted §3.9.2 Note is why: warichu opening brackets are the brackets used for surrounding an inline cutting note (割注), so an occurrence that opens no warichu is not one. §A.28 holds exactly three rows — 0028, 3014 and 005B — and each of the three is also a row of §A.1, which is the shape of a role the same brackets take inside a construct rather than of a second class of the same occurrence. This row is also one of the four whose Character 字形 column prints a full-width compatibility glyph, U+FF3B, against an ASCII UCS value, so the item's text is the ASCII code point. The writing mode is declared because §3.1.1 states that square brackets should be used in horizontal writing mode except for special cases and makes U+3014 〔 their vertical variant; that is a preference weaker than a Remark, both rows carry an empty Remarks cell, and it is recorded here rather than asserted, because nothing in the appendix carries it.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.1, against §A.27's Remarks column and §A.28's construct (§3.9.1, §3.9.2)

forbidden.why: §A.27 lists 005B with the Remarks cell "proportionally-spaced" / 「プロポーショナル」, and this occurrence declares the half em frame §3.1.2 states for cl-01. The frame is what separates two listings of one code point.

cl-28 is membership of a construct: the quoted §3.9.2 Note defines warichu opening brackets as the brackets used for surrounding an inline cutting note (割注), and this input declares no warichu. An implementation that answers cl-28 for every bracket §A.28 lists answers it for ordinary running text, where no cutting note exists to be surrounded.

cases.quote: For example, while this document lists U+0028 LEFT PARENTHESIS as a member of opening brackets (cl-01), the compatibility counterpart U+FF08 FULLWIDTH LEFT PARENTHESIS is used in the Japanese context in most Japanese text layout software. / 例えば，この文書では“U+0028（LEFT PARENTHESIS，始め小括弧）”を始め括弧類（cl-01）の一つに分類しているが，多くの和文組版ソフトウェアでは，和文に適用する場合は対応する互換用の文字コードである“U+FF08（FULLWIDTH LEFT PARENTHESIS）”を使用している．
cases.rationale: The §A preamble Note names this exact pair, so the case rests on the document itself rather than on an inference about compatibility characters in general: U+FF08 is what Japanese text carries, U+0028 is what §A.1 lists, and an implementation that keys Appendix A by code point without folding answers nothing for the commonest spelling of this member in real text, silently. Only the Wide and Narrow decomposition mapping reaches the table; full compatibility folding would fold U+2160 ROMAN NUMERAL ONE, a genuine cl-19 member, onto I. Passing U+FF08 is itself a statement that the frame is full-width, and the item declares it. U+0028 is the appendix's degree-four key — §A.1, §A.25, §A.27 and §A.28 all name it — and three of the four are excluded by facts this input carries: the ideographic frame against §A.27's "proportionally-spaced" Remark, and the absence of any construct against §A.25 単位記号中の文字, characters in a unit symbol, and §A.28, the brackets that surround an inline cutting note.

forbidden.why: §A.27 lists 0028 with the Remarks cell "proportionally-spaced" / 「プロポーショナル」, and §3.9.2's cl-27 Note states the width difference in so many words — Japanese, half em; Western, proportional. This occurrence declares the ideographic frame, which is neither.

cases.quote: To work around this issue, many existing implementations use compatibility characters encoded separately in the standard for the purpose of round-trip integrity with the legacy encoding standards. / この問題に対処するため，多くの実際の処理系では，その他の文字コード規格との往復保全の互換性を維持する目的で規格として別にコード化されている互換用の文字コードを使用している．
cases.rationale: The other half of the same fact, and the one no example in the document spells out. U+FF62 HALFWIDTH LEFT CORNER BRACKET is the compatibility counterpart of §A.1's U+300C, it is the only Narrow decomposition that reaches cl-01, and it is ubiquitous in text that came through a legacy Japanese encoding — which is exactly the round-trip integrity the quoted sentence gives as the reason. The document states the reason generally and gives U+FF08 as its example; the mapping itself is the Unicode Character Database's Decomposition_Type=Wide and Narrow rather than JLReq's, and that provenance is recorded here rather than glossed over. The frame this compatibility code point asserts is half-width, which is also the frame §3.1.2 states for the class, so for the Narrow half the two agree where for U+FF08 they do not.

forbidden.why: The answer of an implementation that folds the Wide decompositions the §A preamble Note names and stops there, leaving U+FF62 unlisted and resolving it by frame. The Note's reason is round-trip integrity with the legacy encoding standards, which is what the half-width forms exist for.

cases.quote: For example, LEFT PARENTHESIS "(" and RIGHT PARENTHESIS ")" has not only different width (Japanese, half em, Western, proportional) but are also different in line position and design. The usage of these two differently designed commas should be explicit. Usually, in a Japanese context Japanese design is used, and in Western context Western design is used.
cases.rationale: The document itself names the axis for this key, and it is the width: Japanese, half em; Western, proportional. This occurrence declares the half em frame, so the §A.27 listing whose Remarks cell reads "proportionally-spaced" does not describe it, and of §A.1, §A.25, §A.27 and §A.28 what survives is §A.1 — cl-25 名 単位記号中の文字 and cl-28 both name characters inside a construct, and this input declares none. The case deliberately does not rest on the Note's closing preference, that in an ambiguous case such as "エディター（editor）は……" the Japanese design is better. That sentence is a preference about which design an author chooses, it is stated about one example, and it is upstream of the frame the caller then declares; once the frame is declared there is nothing left for it to decide. The case below is the same key with the other frame declared.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.1, against §A.27's Remarks column and §3.9.2's cl-27 Note

cases.quote: For example, LEFT PARENTHESIS "(" and RIGHT PARENTHESIS ")" has not only different width (Japanese, half em, Western, proportional) but are also different in line position and design. The usage of these two differently designed commas should be explicit. Usually, in a Japanese context Japanese design is used, and in Western context Western design is used.
cases.rationale: The same code point, the same four Appendix A listings, a different declared frame, and a different class — which is the whole claim, made checkable. §A.27 lists 0028 with the Remarks cell "proportionally-spaced" / 「プロポーショナル」 and the quoted Note gives the width of the Western design as proportional, while §3.1.2 states the advance of a cl-01 member as half-width; a proportional occurrence therefore satisfies §A.27's listing and not §A.1's. An implementation whose classification is a table from code point to class answers this case and the one above identically, and one of the two answers is wrong; there is no font, no measurement and no heuristic involved in telling them apart, only the fact the caller already holds about how they set the character.

forbidden.why: §3.1.2 states that the character advance of opening brackets (cl-01) is half-width, and §3.9.2's cl-27 Note states the Western parenthesis as proportional. An occurrence declared proportional does not satisfy the cl-01 listing, and answering cl-01 for it makes the class a property of the code point, which §A.27's Remarks column exists to deny.

cases.quote: 『 300E LEFT WHITE CORNER BRACKET 始め二重かぎ括弧
cases.rationale: §A.1 holds sixteen keys and every one of them is a single code point: the UCS cell of all sixteen rows is a bare four-hex-digit value, and none is written in the ordered-sequence form the appendix uses elsewhere, as §A.27 does for <02E5, 02E9> and <02E9, 02E5>, which it lists as two distinct members. So two opening brackets that meet are two occurrences and never one key, and the longest match over Appendix A's key structure never crosses them. The input is the assertion: a stream whose items cut a key in half is refused rather than misclassified, so the fact that this five-item stream is well formed is the fact that no cl-01 key spans items 0 and 1. The answer is given for the second bracket, which is the one a scan that merged the pair would lose, and 『 is also the row that follows 「 in the document's order.

cases.quote: JIS X 4051 also provides similar character classes but that are slightly different from this document. Furthermore JIS X 4051 states that it is implementation-defined how to handle characters that are not explicitly mentioned, e.g. whether they should belong to either class or not.
cases.rationale: §A.1's fifteenth row is 00AB LEFT-POINTING DOUBLE ANGLE QUOTATION MARK, 始め二重山括弧引用記号，始めギュメ — the opening double guillemet. Its single counterpart U+2039 SINGLE LEFT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK is in no Appendix A table at all, and it is not reached by folding either, because it has no Wide or Narrow decomposition. That is a boundary the document draws rather than an omission: §A scopes every one of its lists to the non-ideographic characters of ISO/IEC 10646 collections 285 BASIC JAPANESE and 286 JAPANESE NON IDEOGRAPHICS EXTENSION, and the sentence quoted above records that the handling of a character the lists do not mention is implementation-defined and that JLReq inherits that position. So "unlisted" is a real answer for a mark that looks like a member, and any class given for it is a published reading and never a requirement. This occurrence is set with a proportional font, which is the frame on which the two readings differ, so both are recorded with the choice that selects each.

permitted.source: The unconditional reading: every unlisted occurrence is cl-19

forbidden.why: §A.1 lists sixteen keys and 2039 is not one of them. Resemblance to 00AB, which it is listed beside in ISO/IEC 10646 and which §A.1 does list, is not a listing; §3.9.2 records the question as implementation-defined rather than answering it with the nearest table.

cases.quote: JIS X 4051 also provides similar character classes but that are slightly different from this document. Furthermore JIS X 4051 states that it is implementation-defined how to handle characters that are not explicitly mentioned, e.g. whether they should belong to either class or not.
cases.rationale: The same unlisted mark, set full-width in a Japanese line, which is where the two readings of §3.9.2's silence agree. Recording the agreement is what makes the disagreement above legible: the frame is the only thing separating them, so an implementation that answers cl-19 here and cl-19 there has not implemented the by-frame reading at all, it has implemented the unconditional one, and the pair of cases says which without either of them having to name an implementation. The by-frame reading extends the one distinction the document itself draws over text its tables do not enumerate — §3.2.4 sets full-width and fixed-width Western characters as quasi Japanese characters, §3.2.6 gives proportionally set Western text the composition rules of cl-27 — and the frame is the fact an unlisted occurrence still carries.

permitted.source: The unconditional reading: every unlisted occurrence is cl-19
